correctness.rationale: The repaired RESULT.md proves exactly 32 complete mappings on the full labeled nine-element semigroup. Injectivity of x↦xα(x) forces α(0)=0 and the first index of α(i,g,j) to equal j. For a fixed (i,j), coincident output indices on the two g inputs would force complementary α bits and equal product bits, a contradiction. Hence k=g+s_ij. At fixed (j,k) the two i inputs must have distinct α bits, so h=i+f_jk. For each (i,k), product injectivity is precisely s_i0+s_i1+f_0k+f_1k=1. A common row difference d and four free bits s_00,s_10,f_00,f_01 determine every solution uniquely, proving 32. Independently, python3 /workspace/reproductions/brandt.py enumerated 576 choices of two local permutations for the product bijection, recovered the unique right multiplier for each input, and found 16 admissible first blocks with two followers each. For the retained contextual all-even construction, the quotient coordinates are recovered by subtraction modulo t and the bits by addition modulo two; both α and the product map are bijective also at t=1. The proof uses no extrapolation from the finite calculation.

value.rationale: The repaired result gives a full labeled transversal total at the first index where the Brandt semigroup over the smallest nontrivial group admits complete mappings although the group itself does not. The obstruction threshold motivates this specific object and invariant independently of the computation. The exact total and its five-bit classification are reusable small benchmarks for enumeration of complete mappings of group-bearing Rees zero-matrix semigroups. No new value is claimed for reproducing the known existence theorem or construction, and the count is not generalized to all even n.
